title: Glad I Found this Sub
content: I've been trying to regain my lucid dreaming skills that I had when I was a teenager. I originally started LDs so I could stop recurring nightmares I was having if witches and monsters hunting me. It worked a treat as I was able to just banish them. I started lucid dreaming every night and after about a year intentionally stopped as it was fatiguing. Now I'm much older and struggling to get it back so that I can create a portal into the astral from my lucid dream. I make dream notes a lot and can often remember 6+ dreams per night. I've noticed that there are some places which are recurring which align with what is written here. I believe they are shared spaces where the great majority of people are actually dreaming and not conscious. They look different to each of us as our subconscious interprets it individually differently so we can make sense of it. Whenever it is a school, office building or shopping centre it's a shared space. I also am convinced it's in the astral plane. I've become lucid there a few times and tried to create portals to the astral and can't....because I'm already there. This lines up with many astral projectors who say that some places they go to are full of people dreaming who just go about their business and are extremely hard to make lucid. If they manage to make them lucid they usually vanish as they're waking up in their body. They also report that in this place most of the dreamers are attending lessons in morality and other things. One of the most powerful experiences was when I was in an office building and the people in charge told me it was time to test me. They say me down in a classroom in front of a computer and made me do a series of linked tests in a storyline of earth being attacked. To progress I had to pass each chapter. I had to create a team of people to fight back and at our first battle we lost. They asked me why we lost and I said we needed a new weapon...they asked what it was and after some thinking I said "love, love is the answer". They stopped the test and said I'd passed.
